_about: Prose facts the prototype shows beside the counts of facts.json: streams, lanes, blockers, decisions, decided items and the since list. Each entry names its source (file and line, or command) and the time it was read. Nothing here is a number the page computes; counts come from facts.json only.
deliverable: CodeFlow 4.0.0: every task of its three epics lands on the integration line with its review, the line passes one full gate and the journey on the installed candidate, and one pull request from the line into main is ready for the operator to merge.
deliverableSource: EPC-022.md Summary, the 'Done means' sentence (line 30 to 34 on the line)
basis: One percent basis everywhere: complete tasks over all tasks of EPC-022, EPC-024 and EPC-025 on the integration line, cancelled tasks excluded. A task is on main only when its own record on origin/main says complete; otherwise it is complete on the line only. A task is in a pull request when an open pull request against the line names it in its branch name.

inputs.title: The view tree: outcomes first, then the cross-cutting views
inputs.context: The side menu's first area opens on the Overview and lists the three outcomes (one per epic); each opens to its themes (the epic's amendment sections) and each theme to its tasks. Epics, Lanes, Blockers, What changed, Evidence, Decisions, Script and Report kinds cut across.

options.label: Approve the tree as shown
options.cost: none; the dashboard shell (TSK-1120) and the status document (TSK-1098) take it as written in their amendments

options.label: Drop the theme level: outcome opens straight to its tasks
options.cost: one record change; the 220 tasks of the 4.0.0 milestone fixes (EPC-022) become one list under its outcome

options.label: Another order or grouping; say which
options.cost: one more prototype round with renders

inputs.reasoning: The theme level is the grouping the status facts command (TSK-1095 AC-15) already defines (the record section that introduced the task), so it costs nothing to compute and it keeps the 220-task list readable.

inputs.title: Tabs inside an outcome: Progress, Order, Issues
inputs.context: Decision d2 chose three tabs per topic. The prototype shows Progress (percent, partition and themes), Order (the tasks in dependency order with their next-step reasons) and Issues (blocked, waiting and open pull requests for that epic).

options.label: Keep three tabs under other names; say which
options.cost: a wording change in the status document task (TSK-1098 AC-10)

inputs.reasoning: The three tabs answer the brief's questions 6, 3 and 4 inside one outcome without leaving it.

inputs.title: The task context strip: which facts lead
inputs.context: A task view opens with a strip of labelled facts: outcome, location, lane, state, window, last moved, pull request (the status document, TSK-1098 AC-10). The prototype draws outcome, theme, location, state, record last changed and pull request; lane and window read `not recorded` until the status facts command (TSK-1095) lands them.

options.label: Keep the strip as drawn; `not recorded` stays visible
Hide a fact the facts do not carry
options.cost: a reader cannot tell a missing fact from an omitted one

inputs.reasoning: The status facts command (TSK-1095 AC-15) says `not recorded`, never invented and never blank; the strip shows the rule.

inputs.title: Change marks since the previous report
inputs.context: Numbers that moved since the report of 14:31 EST, 1 Nov carry a small delta beside them, and the menu dots the views with a change. Revision in place (TSK-1121) computes these from the previous revision of the same topic.

options.label: Keep the delta beside the number and the dot in the menu
Only the What changed view, no inline marks
options.cost: a reader must leave the view to know what moved

inputs.reasoning: An inline delta is the smallest mark that answers question 5 where the reader already is.
